about: Trainchecker 'Your train passes near…'. One item per stretch between neighbouring stations. side is the side of the train when travelling from a to b (facing forwards); swap left/right for b to a. text has {side} for 'left'/'right'; textReverse, where present, replaces text for b to a. England only. Researched in a Claude chat, November 22nd 2026; every fact checked against source.

lines.name: London Paddington to Bristol Temple Meads via Bath
Reading to Penzance via Newbury, Westbury, Taunton, Exeter and Plymouth

items.name: Kensal Green Cemetery
items.text: Your train passes near Kensal Green Cemetery, on the train's {side}, where Isambard Kingdom Brunel, the engineer who built this railway, is buried with his father, Marc.

items.name: Ealing Village
items.text: Your train passes near Ealing Village, on the train's {side}: five Art Deco blocks of flats built from 1934 to 1936 to tempt film stars from Ealing Studios. In the end, most of the flats went to film crews.

items.name: Pitzhanger Manor
items.text: Your train passes near Pitzhanger Manor, on the train's {side}, the country house that the architect Sir John Soane designed and built for himself between 1800 and 1804.

items.name: Kensington and Chelsea Cemetery, Hanwell
items.text: Your train passes near the Kensington and Chelsea cemetery in Hanwell, on the train's {side}, opened in 1855. One of its tombs, for the shell expert Edgar Smith, is decorated with a large conch shell.

items.name: Wharncliffe Viaduct
items.text: Your train crosses the Wharncliffe Viaduct over the Brent valley, Isambard Kingdom Brunel's first major design for the railway, built in 1836 and 1837. Lord Wharncliffe's coat of arms is carved on its south side.

items.name: Gurdwara Sri Guru Singh Sabha
items.text: Your train passes near Gurdwara Sri Guru Singh Sabha, on the train's {side}. When it opened in 2003, Guinness World Records named it the largest Sikh temple outside India.

items.name: Old Vinyl Factory
items.text: Your train passes near the Old Vinyl Factory, on the train's {side}: EMI's old record works, which pressed vinyl records from 1952 until the 1970s.

items.name: River Colne
items.text: Your train crosses the River Colne, and about here passes between Greater London and Buckinghamshire.

items.name: Buckinghamshire and Berkshire
items.text: Between Iver and Langley, your train passes from Buckinghamshire into Berkshire.
items.textReverse: Between Langley and Iver, your train passes from Berkshire into Buckinghamshire.

items.name: Kedermister Library, St Mary's Church, Langley
items.text: Your train passes near St Mary's Church, Langley, on the train's {side}. Inside is the Kedermister Library, a parish library from the 1600s still kept in the painted cupboards made for it in 1620.

items.name: Site of William Herschel's house
items.text: Your train passes near the site of William Herschel's house, on the train's {side}, where he and his sister Caroline built his 40-foot telescope, the largest in the world for 50 years. With it he found two of Saturn's moons in 1789.

items.name: Burnham Abbey
items.text: Your train passes near Burnham Abbey, on the train's {side}, founded in 1266 by Richard, Earl of Cornwall, brother of King Henry III. Anglican nuns made it their home from 1916.

items.name: Maidenhead Railway Bridge
items.text: Your train crosses the Thames on Brunel's Maidenhead Railway Bridge, whose two main brick arches are thought to be the longest and flattest ever built. Turner painted a train crossing it in Rain, Steam and Speed (1844).

items.name: Church of St James, Ruscombe
items.text: Your train passes near the Church of St James, Ruscombe, on the train's {side}. Its flint chancel dates from the 12th century; the nave and tower were rebuilt in brick in 1638 and 1639.

items.name: Reading Abbey
items.text: Your train passes near the ruins of Reading Abbey, on the train's {side}, founded by Henry I in 1121. He was buried there in 1136.

items.name: Chazey Court Barn
items.text: Your train passes near Chazey Court Barn, on the train's {side} across the Thames: a huge seven-bay brick barn from about 1700, listed Grade I.

items.name: Mapledurham Watermill
items.text: Your train passes near Mapledurham Watermill, on the train's {side} across the Thames, the last working watermill on the river.

items.name: Basildon Park
items.text: Your train passes near Basildon Park, on the train's {side}, an 18th-century house that played Netherfield, Mr Bingley's home, in the 2005 film of Pride & Prejudice.

items.name: Moulsford Railway Bridge
items.text: Your train crosses the Thames on Moulsford Railway Bridge, known locally as Four Arches. Brunel set its brick arches at a slant across the river.

items.name: St Mary's Church, Cholsey
items.text: Your train passes near St Mary's Church, Cholsey, on the train's {side}, where Agatha Christie is buried.

items.name: Uffington
items.text: Your train passes near the village of Uffington, on the train's {side}, where Thomas Hughes, author of Tom Brown's School Days, was born in 1822. The poet John Betjeman lived there from 1934 to 1945.

items.name: STEAM, Museum of the Great Western Railway
items.text: Your train passes near STEAM, the Museum of the Great Western Railway, on the train's {side}. It is in a workshop of Swindon Works, built around 1842 with stone from Box Tunnel.

items.name: Central Government War Headquarters, Corsham
items.text: While your train is in Box Tunnel, the government's secret Cold War headquarters, built in an old stone quarry, lies just to the train's {side}.

items.name: Roman Baths
items.text: Your train passes near the Roman Baths, on the train's {side}, where the Romans built a temple at the hot spring between AD 60 and 70.

items.name: Saltford Brass Mill
items.text: Your train passes near Saltford Brass Mill, on the train's {side}, the last survivor of more than 30 mills that once worked along this stretch of the Avon.

items.name: Somerdale
items.text: Your train passes near the old Somerdale chocolate factory, on the train's {side}, built for Fry's from 1924 and closed in 2011. Remains of a Roman settlement were found on the site.

items.name: Greyfriars Church, Reading
items.text: Your train passes near Greyfriars Church, on the train's {side}, the oldest Franciscan church in the UK still used for worship.

items.name: Garston Lock
items.text: Your train passes near Garston Lock, on the train's {side}, one of only two working turf-sided locks left on the Kennet and Avon Canal. Its sloping grass sides use more water than brick ones.

items.name: Folly Farm, Sulhamstead
items.text: Your train passes near Folly Farm, on the train's {side}, a house that Edwin Lutyens extended around 1906 and 1912, with gardens he designed with Gertrude Jekyll.

items.name: Aldermaston Lock
items.text: Your train passes near Aldermaston Lock, on the train's {side}, built between 1718 and 1723 and later given unusual scalloped brick walls.

items.name: Midgham Lock
items.text: Your train passes near Midgham Lock, on the train's {side}, one of the locks built between 1718 and 1723 under the engineer John Hore of Newbury, when the River Kennet was made navigable.

items.name: Monkey Marsh Lock
items.text: Your train passes near Monkey Marsh Lock, on the train's {side}, a turf-sided lock from the 1720s that is now a scheduled monument.

items.name: West Berkshire Museum
items.text: Your train passes near the West Berkshire Museum, on the train's {side}, partly housed in Newbury's Cloth Hall, built in 1627 as a cloth factory.

items.name: Litten Chapel
items.text: Your train passes near the Litten Chapel, on the train's {side}, an early 16th-century chapel of Newbury's medieval St Bartholomew's hospital, with finely carved timber roof trusses.

items.name: Church of St Mark and St Luke, Avington
items.text: Your train passes near the church of St Mark and St Luke at Avington, on the train's {side}, an unspoilt Norman church listed Grade I.

items.name: Somerset Hospital, Froxfield
items.text: Your train passes near the Somerset Hospital at Froxfield, on the train's {side}: almshouses for widows left by Sarah, Duchess of Somerset, the oldest part built in 1694.

items.name: Crofton Pumping Station
items.text: Your train passes Crofton Pumping Station, on the train's {side}. Its Boulton & Watt steam engine of 1812 is the oldest working beam engine in the world still in its original engine house.

items.name: Edington Priory
items.text: Your train passes near Edington Priory church, on the train's {side}, built by William Edington, Bishop of Winchester, and consecrated in 1361.

items.name: Witham Priory
items.text: Your train passes the site of Witham Priory, on the train's {side}, founded in 1178 or 1179 as the first Carthusian monastery in England.

items.name: Bruton Dovecote
items.text: Your train passes near the Bruton Dovecote, on the train's {side}, a stone tower built between the 15th and 17th centuries that may have been a lookout before it housed pigeons.

items.name: Athelney
items.text: Your train passes near Athelney, on the train's {side}, where Alfred the Great hid before defeating the Vikings at Edington in 878, and where he later founded an abbey.

items.name: Tonedale Mills, Wellington
items.text: Your train passes near Tonedale Mills in Wellington, on the train's {side}, the largest textile mill in South West England, famous for Taunton serge and later the khaki cloth and puttees of the British Army.

items.name: St Andrew's Church, Cullompton
items.text: Your train passes near St Andrew's Church, Cullompton, on the train's {side}, mostly 15th-century and known for its fan-vaulted Lane Aisle.

items.name: Exeter Cathedral
items.text: Your train passes near Exeter Cathedral, on the train's {side}, complete by about 1400, with the longest unbroken medieval stone-vaulted ceiling in the world.

items.name: Custom House, Exeter
items.text: Your train passes near Exeter's Custom House, on the train's {side}, built in the late 17th century, the first in England built for the purpose.

items.name: Powderham Castle
items.text: Your train passes near Powderham Castle, on the train's {side}, a fortified manor house on the bank of the Exe estuary, listed Grade I.

items.name: Starcross Pumping House
items.text: Your train passes Brunel's pumping house at Starcross, on the train's {side}, built in 1845 for his atmospheric railway, whose trains ran for less than a year. It is the only complete pumping house left from the three atmospheric lines in the British Isles.

items.name: Langstone Rock
items.text: Your train passes Langstone Rock, on the train's {side}, a red sandstone headland that the sea, and then Brunel's railway, cut off from the mainland.

items.name: Parson and Clerk
items.text: As your train goes through Parson's Tunnel, the two rock stacks it is named after, the Parson and Clerk, stand just off the headland on the train's {side}.

items.name: Shaldon
items.text: Your train runs beside the Teign estuary, with the village of Shaldon across the water on the train's {side}.

items.name: Forde House, Newton Abbot
items.text: Your train passes near Forde House, on the train's {side}, a manor house of about 1550, enlarged around 1610 and known for its 17th-century carving and plasterwork.

items.name: Totnes Castle
items.text: Your train passes near Totnes Castle, on the train's {side}, one of the best-preserved Norman motte-and-bailey castles in England.

items.name: Saltram House
items.text: Your train passes near Saltram House, on the train's {side}, which Nikolaus Pevsner called "the most impressive country house in Devon", with interiors by Robert Adam.

items.name: Mount Pleasant Redoubt
items.text: Your train passes near Mount Pleasant Redoubt, on the train's {side}, an earthwork fort built around 1780 to guard the dockyard against a French and Spanish invasion.

items.name: Devonport Park
items.text: Your train passes near Devonport Park, on the train's {side}, laid out in the 1850s on former military land.

items.name: HMNB Devonport
items.text: Your train passes near Devonport naval base, on the train's {side}, the largest naval base in Western Europe.

items.name: HMS Drake
items.text: Your train passes near HMS Drake, on the train's {side}: not a ship but a "stone frigate", the naval barracks for Devonport.

items.name: Royal Albert Bridge
items.text: Your train crosses the Tamar from Devon into Cornwall on Brunel's Royal Albert Bridge, its two 455-foot iron spans 100 feet above the water.
items.textReverse: Your train crosses the Tamar from Cornwall into Devon on Brunel's Royal Albert Bridge, its two 455-foot iron spans 100 feet above the water.

items.name: Trematon Castle
items.text: Your train passes near Trematon Castle, on the train's {side}, a Norman motte-and-bailey castle with a 12th-century keep, overlooking the River Lynher.

items.name: St Germans Priory
items.text: Your train passes near St Germans church, on the train's {side}, once the seat of the Saxon bishops of Cornwall.

items.name: St Martin's Church, Liskeard
items.text: Your train passes near St Martin's Church, Liskeard, on the train's {side}, the second-largest parish church in Cornwall.

items.name: Moorswater Viaduct
items.text: Your train crosses Moorswater Viaduct. Beside it stand the stone piers of the earlier viaduct, which carried the line on timber, as Brunel advised for Cornwall's valleys.

items.name: Restormel Castle
items.text: Your train passes near Restormel Castle, on the train's {side}, a Norman castle known for its perfectly circular design.

items.name: Duchy Palace, Lostwithiel
items.text: Your train passes near the Duchy Palace in Lostwithiel, on the train's {side}, once the centre from which the Dukes of Cornwall ran their estates.

items.name: Charlestown
items.text: Your train passes near Charlestown harbour, on the train's {side}, a port that grew in the late 18th century from the fishing village of West Polmear and has changed little since.

items.name: Truro Cathedral
items.text: Your train passes near Truro Cathedral, on the train's {side}, built between 1880 and 1910 on the site of St Mary's parish church.

items.name: Wheal Busy
items.text: Your train passes near Wheal Busy, on the train's {side}, a mine that produced huge amounts of copper in the 18th century, now part of the Cornish mining World Heritage Site.

items.name: Carn Brea
items.text: Your train passes near the hill of Carn Brea, on the train's {side}, with a Neolithic enclosure, a medieval castle and old mine workings on it.

items.name: Trevithick Cottage
items.text: Your train passes near Trevithick Cottage, on the train's {side}, childhood home of the Cornish engineer Richard Trevithick, now cared for by the National Trust.

items.name: Harvey & Co foundry, Hayle
items.text: Your train passes the old offices of Harvey & Co, on the train's {side}, the foundry John Harvey set up in Hayle in 1779.

items.name: Penzance Heliport
items.text: Your train passes near Penzance Heliport, on the train's {side}, where helicopters to the Isles of Scilly started flying again in 2020 after an eight-year gap.

items.name: Didcot Railway Centre
items.text: Your train passes Didcot Railway Centre, on the train's {side}, a railway museum in what was once a Great Western Railway engine shed.

items.name: Appleford Railway Bridge
items.text: Your train crosses the Thames on Appleford Railway Bridge. The first bridge here, of timber, was finished in 1844; today's steel one dates from 1927.

items.name: Culham fusion research site
items.text: Your train passes near the Culham fusion research site, on the train's {side}. Its Joint European Torus began work in 1983 and in 1991 became the first reactor in the world to run on the deuterium and tritium fuel meant for future power stations.

items.name: St Mary the Virgin, Iffley
items.text: Your train passes near St Mary the Virgin, Iffley, on the train's {side}, built in the second half of the 12th century and one of the best-preserved Norman churches in England.

items.name: Elm Park (stadium site)
items.text: Your train passes near the site of Elm Park, on the train's {side}, home of Reading Football Club from 1896 to 1998.

items.name: Mortimer station
items.text: Mortimer station, at one end of this stretch, keeps its Brunel-designed Great Western Railway buildings, still in use.

items.name: Holy Ghost Chapel ruins, Basingstoke
items.text: Your train passes near the ruins of the Holy Ghost Chapel, on the train's {side}: a chapel stood here by 1244, and Lord Sandys added a family chapel in 1524.

items.name: Loddon Nature Reserve
items.text: Your train passes near Loddon Nature Reserve, on the train's {side}, 14 hectares run by the Berks, Bucks and Oxon Wildlife Trust.

items.name: Hannen Columbarium, Wargrave
items.text: Your train passes near St Mary's churchyard in Wargrave, on the train's {side}, where the Hannen family's columbarium, a resting place for ashes, was designed by Edwin Lutyens.

items.name: Henley Bridge
items.text: Your train passes near Henley Bridge, on the train's {side}, built in 1786 with five stone arches across the Thames.
